conviction_note: Findings sum to +1.4 (Walmart's $6B EMAA and a crowded short against a Q1-guide risk vs a $817.5M consensus and a cash-flow test), but the 8.7-pt put skew, beats sold on the last two prints (-14.9%, -7.7%) and a +39% squeeze last November leave the sign close to a coin flip: p_up 51 on an abs move of 14.5 (implied 13.1, history median 13.8, raised for the new Q1 guide/EMAA quantification and 10 days to cover), so the scaled number is +0.29, well under the findings sum because the skew and the reaction history argue the other way.
bar: FQ4 revenue: company guide $760-780M and adj. EBITDA $100-105M (Q3 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001837240/000183724026000042/q3268-k_ex991.htm); consensus $773.9M / non-GAAP EPS $0.16 (Earnings Whispers via https://finviz.com/news/422875/symbotics-q4-guide-promises-acceleration-but-a-20-stock-slide-demands-cash-proof, 2026-11-15), Benzinga $773.8M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SYM/earnings-forecasts). Next-quarter bar: FQ1 FY27 revenue consensus about $817.5M, EPS $0.13 (Benzinga, single source family, so findings resting on it are capped small). Management also promised positive Q4 free cash flow on the Aug 5 call.
positioning_check: Short interest 17,535,719 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, down 159k from 17.69M on 10-15, up from 15.35M at 07-31; days to cover 10.2 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sym/shortinterest). Percent of float is not reliably sourced: Benzinga shows 31.7-40.5% of float (undated, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SYM/short-interest); against ~600M total shares incl. Class V it is ~3%, so the Class A float short is likely high (tens of percent). Crowded short by days-to-cover. Skew: +8.74 vol points 25d put over call, downside paid; put/call OI 0.59. Stock 58% below its 52-week high, +6.0% over 5 days, -4.1% over 20 days, down about 13.6% month-to-date as of 2026-11-17 (AAII). SoftBank fully exited its Class A in May 2026, removing a seller overhang.

findings.finding: Symbotic and Walmart signed an Enterprise Master Automation Agreement on 2026-10-29 with an initial ~$6.0B commitment (Symbotic says it could add up to $6.92B to backlog, against a $22.5B backlog that has sat at $22.3-22.7B for a year), plus $125M of Walmart-funded R&D, covering 25 US regional DCs (BreakPack, SymMicro) and select Americas international sites; the commitment cannot be reduced without mutual consent and has a shortfall payment if Walmart buys fewer systems. It was signed after the FQ4 period ended, so tonight's call is the first time management can put timing, revenue conversion and a pro forma backlog (~$29B) on it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog/visibility news last carried the November 2025 print (+39.4%, with a flat Q1 guide); backlog stagnation was cited around the Aug 2026 print (-14.9%). The EMAA itself got about +1.9% pre-market on 2026-10-30 (RTTNews) and the stock then fell into mid-November.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but the stock is below the pre-announcement level (~$37.4 on 10-29 vs $36.33 now, after trading near $32.8 on 11-17), so the market has given it no credit: no timing, no conversion rate, no margin, and it adds to concentration (Walmart >90% of revenue, two board observers). If it were priced as a ~30% backlog step-up with near-term conversion, the stock would not be at its post-earnings low area with downside skew bid.
findings.independence: Press release (same agreement): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001837240/000119312526437874/d182210dex991.htm ; pre-market reaction https://www.rttnews.com/3706213/symbotic-expands-walmart-automation-deal-with-6-bln-initial-spending-commitment.aspx . All describe one document.

findings.finding: The FQ1 FY27 guide risks landing below the ~$817.5M revenue consensus: management said about 15% of the $22.5B backlog converts in the next 12 months (~$3.4B, ~$845M a quarter on average across a rising ramp), Q4 system starts would be 'a little short' of Q3's 11, revenue per deployment has fallen four quarters running, and last year's Q1 guide ($610-630M) was flat to the Q4 actual ($618M), so a midpoint near $790-810M is plausible against an $817.5M bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has carried this stock: Nov 2025 Q1 guide flat vs Q4 but margin/EBITDA up, +39.4%; Aug 2026 Q4 guide $760-780M with flat EBITDA margin and backlog down, -14.9%; May 2026 -7.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $817.5M assumes Q4's ~7% sequential growth continues, while the company's own conversion, starts and Q1-seasonality statements point a little lower. If this were priced, the Q1 estimate would sit near $800M rather than $817.5M. It is an inference from management statements, not a company number, and the bar has one source family, so it is capped small.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 guide vs Q4 FY25 actual: https://www.tikr.com/blog/symbotic-nasdsq-sym-stock-surges-on-strong-outlook-for-q1-of-2026 ; Q1 FY27 consensus: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SYM/earnings-forecasts . The EMAA (finding 1) could offset it if any of it converts in Q1.

findings.finding: On the reported quarter the company has landed at or just above the top of its revenue range (Q1 FY26 $630M vs $610-630M; Q3 $721M vs $700-720M) and beat EBITDA guidance (Q3 $95M vs $80-85M), which implies FQ4 revenue around $780M against a $774M consensus and EBITDA above $105M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold: Aug 2026 revenue at the top of the range and an EBITDA beat, -14.9%; EPS missed in 3 of the last 4 quarters (Benzinga).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus already sits in the upper half of the guide. What is left is the small gap between landing at the top of the range and the $774M figure, inside what the company guided.

findings.finding: Short interest is 17.5M shares with 10.2 days to cover (2026-10-30 settlement), near its high for the year, in a stock 58% below its 52-week high whose last November print rose 39%. Any clean guide/cash print has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 +39.4% into high short interest; but Aug 2026 -14.9% and Feb 2025 -15.9% show the short is not one-way.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew is bid for downside (+8.7 pts) and put/call OI 0.59, so options price the downside; the asymmetric cover-driven upside of a 10-day-to-cover short is not in the skew.

findings.finding: Peer AutoStore reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05 (after Symbotic last spoke): order intake USD 178M, +17% YoY, revenue +38%, and raised its FY2026 revenue guide to ~USD 750M from ~USD 700M, a sign that warehouse-automation demand is healthy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of SYM reacting to peer prints; SYM revenue is >90% Walmart, so the transmission is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy, not a counterparty, so it is small. If the market read it across, SYM would not be down ~13% month-to-date into mid-November.
findings.independence: Proxy only; none from a different source.

findings.finding: The anchor customer Walmart (about 90% of SYM revenue) beat and raised on 2026-11-19 (Q3 FY27 revenue $188.8B, +5.2%; FY27 sales growth guide raised to 4.9-5.2% cc; US e-commerce +23%), with supply-chain investment credited. No automation capex detail was found, and in Feb 2026 Walmart had called FY27 the peak year for automation spending.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for SYM on Walmart prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Counterparty health is a weak signal for SYM's timing, so it is small. The 'peak automation capex' remark (Feb 2026) has been public for nine months and is offset by the October EMAA.

findings.finding: Cash test: Q3 free cash flow was -$164.6M (cash $2.0B to $1.7B), which management blamed on the timing of receipts tied to project starts, and it promised positive Q4 FCF. But Q4 starts were guided 'a little short' of Q3, so start-linked receipts may not rebound much. Previews call cash the simplest test of the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026 print with negative FCF and falling cash: -14.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The promise is public, and so is the doubt (the Earnings Whispers preview headline). The fewer-starts link to receipts is an inference. Shrunk because the short is crowded and a delivered positive FCF would cut the other way.
findings.independence: Call transcript (starts 'a little short of the third', FCF 'timing'): https://www.webull.com/news/15393402869851136 ; preview: https://finviz.com/news/422875/symbotics-q4-guide-promises-acceleration-but-a-20-stock-slide-demands-cash-proof . Shares the transcript with finding 2.

findings.finding: Material weaknesses over revenue recognition and cost timing persisted through FQ2 FY26, with remediation tied to an ERP rollout in FY27, so the FY26 10-K and the release may again carry them (Hunterbrook was short on the earlier delayed 10-K).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2024 revenue-recognition restatement and delayed 10-K caused a sharp fall; since then, persistence of the weakness has not visibly moved a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely known and expected to persist until FY27; only a new error or a delayed 10-K would matter, and nothing points to one. Filing date of the 10-K unverified (may fall after the window).

baseline_tension: The sum leans slightly positive on the EMAA and the crowded short, against a +8.7-pt put skew and two straight sold prints. The evidence does not beat the skew decisively, so p_up stays near 50.
